neighbours.label: The ' up' after jump or leap (jump up, leap up, jumps up); 'looks up' and other movement stay low.
fire: The pony jumps up to four feet with no effort.
The memories leap up and catch me off guard.
She invited the children to jump up on the bench with her.
To reach the shelf, just jump up onto the crate.
The two goalkeepers jump up and try to punch the ball.
The dog leaped up and licked my face.
He jumped up from his chair when the phone rang.
Salmon leap up the falls every autumn.
quiet: The pony looks up at the fence with no fear.
The memories wake me up and keep me awake.
She invited the children to line up by the bench with her.
To reach the shelf, just pick up the crate.
The two goalkeepers warm up and try to relax.
The dog woke up and licked my face.
He stood up from his chair when the phone rang.
Salmon swim up the river every autumn.

predictions: 8/8 fire, 0-1 near miss. Coverage partial: ' out' x5, ' on' x3 on the card.
notes: Probes: 0.57-0.84 on jump up and leap up; 'looks up' 0.02. Near misses keep ' up' with other verbs, which the probes tested only once.
